title: Ship JetBrains adapter distribution host
description: Objective: land one real JetBrains host/distribution consumer for the thin adapter so portability evidence can certify an installed artifact rather than its unit-test shape. Deliverable: a minimal plugin/host launcher that imports @moe/jetbrains-adapter, discovers the signed IDE_ADAPTER distribution component, connects to the standalone control room, and preserves teardown/reconnect semantics. NOT in scope: rendering a second UI, lifecycle authority, or packaging other IDEs. Measured at HEAD 30458af: createJetBrainsSession/admitDistribution are public from @moe/jetbrains-adapter (task-9fd52b41f3ea4aad8c0c07bbe6fd3025), but all callers are adapter tests and distribution integration labels IDE_ADAPTER only as a fixture, not a shipped artifact. Consumer: task-22cfca91c5134b24aaf3e5734444fb93. Owned paths: a focused JetBrains host/plugin subtree, adapters/jetbrains package wiring/tests, and packaging asset inventory paths.
definitionOfDone: A production JetBrains host imports createJetBrainsSession from the bare @moe/jetbrains-adapter root and implements only daemon discovery/start, control-room open, and uninstall/reconnect ports; it contains no lifecycle reducer, command authorization, or board rendering.

Distribution packaging includes a real IDE_ADAPTER component with exact source SHA/schema/compatibility/tool/asset digests and JetBrains startup rejects stale/incompatible sets with DISTRIBUTION_MISMATCH before daemon access.
A compiled bare-specifier probe verifies the host manifest dependency and pnpm-lock importer; a plain-runtime test loads the shipped adapter/host without Vitest path rewriting.

Focused tests pin exact JetBrains/IDE/distribution code and layer for absent, stale, start-unverified, open-unknown, concurrent open, and uninstall races, plus one successful reconnect/control-room handoff.
JetBrains/package and distribution integration gates exit 0.
taskRails: Keep the IDE shell thin; the standalone control room remains the only UI.
Do not fabricate an IDE_ADAPTER distribution with a test fixture or placeholder bytes.
Use official daemon/MCP/HTTP surfaces only; no custom transport.

implementationPlan.description: TDD red for the four real ports, in a new adapters/jetbrains/src/host/jetbrains-host.test.ts. Each port converts a fact about the real world into ONE evidence arm, and every case pins the exact arm plus the exact code and layer the adapter then produces — never merely that it failed. DISTRIBUTION DISCOVERY: an install root with well-formed manifest documents yields those manifests in order; a root that does not exist, an unreadable entry, or a document that is not JSON yields an EMPTY set rather than a partial one, because admitDistribution refuses an empty set with DISTRIBUTION_MISMATCH and a partial set would silently drop the component that was supposed to be missing. DAEMON DISCOVERY: a listening endpoint yields {status:"LISTENING", endpoint}; connection refused yields NOT_LISTENING; a timeout or any other transport fault yields UNDETERMINED with a detail that contains no credential and no host path. An HTTP 401 MUST be treated as LISTENING — the probe observes reachability only and must not carry a credential, so an authenticated refusal is proof the daemon is up. START: a spawn that is confirmed listening within the bound yields LISTENING_CONFIRMED with the endpoint; a spawn that returns but never confirms yields LAUNCHED_UNCONFIRMED; a spawn that cannot be launched yields REFUSED — and the confirm loop must be BOUNDED, with the bound asserted, or an unreachable daemon hangs the IDE. CONTROL ROOM: assets present plus a successful OS open yields {assets:"PRESENT", embedded:"UNAVAILABLE", browser:{status:"OPENED"}}; assets missing yields {assets:"ABSENT"}; the host NEVER reports embedded:"OPENED" because it renders nothing. Assert a hand-written case count. Run and record the RED.

THE PORTS ARE EXERCISED AGAINST REAL RESOURCES, not doubles — a scripted double would satisfy every assertion here while the production port still failed on contact with the OS:
  - real `node:fs` temp install roots via mkdtempSync(tmpdir()) (never a literal /tmp — that resolves to D:\tmp from this repo and does not exist)
  - real `node:http` servers on 127.0.0.1:0 for 200 / 401 / never-responds
  - a real released port for a genuine ECONNREFUSED
  - real child processes: one that actually listens, one that spawns and exits without listening, one command that does not exist
  Only the OS browser opener is injected, because a test cannot open a real browser.

EVERY CASE PINS CODE + OUTCOME + REFUSING LAYER, via the production `decide*` functions, never a re-implemented helper:
  distribution  manifests-in-order | root-absent | unreadable-entry | not-json  (empty-on-fault, never partial)
  discovery     LISTENING(200) and LISTENING(401) -> OK/DAEMON_RUNNING/layer null; NOT_LISTENING -> OK/DAEMON_ABSENT; UNDETERMINED -> UNKNOWN/DAEMON_STATE_UNKNOWN/DAEMON_DISCOVERY_PORT
  start         LISTENING_CONFIRMED -> OK/DAEMON_STARTED/null; LAUNCHED_UNCONFIRMED -> UNKNOWN/DAEMON_START_UNVERIFIED/IDE_ADAPTER (the measured layer, correcting the plan); REFUSED -> REFUSED/DAEMON_START_REFUSED/DAEMON_START_PORT
  control room  browser OPENED -> OK/CONTROL_ROOM_BROWSER_FALLBACK; assets ABSENT -> REFUSED/CONTROL_ROOM_ASSETS_MISSING/CONTROL_ROOM_OPEN_PORT; opener throws -> REFUSED/CONTROL_ROOM_BROWSER_REFUSED/CONTROL_ROOM_OPEN_PORT

THREE GUARDS THE PLAN ASKED FOR, ALL PRESENT:
  1. The 401 case is a POSITIVE reachability case, not a refusal — the probe carries no credential, so an authenticated refusal proves the daemon is up. Mapping it to REFUSED would start a second daemon beside a healthy one (drill D3).
  2. The confirm loop is bounded on BOTH sides: production has confirmTimeoutMs, and every awaited port call is wrapped in a local `bounded()` that rejects with `bounded wait expired: <what>`. Removing the production bound therefore produces a NAMED failure instead of a stalled suite (drill D4).
  3. The UNDETERMINED case probes an endpoint carrying a real credential — `http://user:s3cr3t-probe-token@127.0.0.1:<port>/` — and asserts the detail contains none of the token, the host, the port, or `://`. Sanitization is proven against a secret that is actually present, not asserted in the abstract.
  Plus: assets-ABSENT asserts the opener recorded ZERO calls, so "refuses before touching the OS" is measured rather than ordered by luck.

SWEEP VACUITY GUARD: `COVERED_ARMS` is a hand-written list of 14 arms; each case calls record(arm) and a final test asserts the EXECUTED set equals the list exactly (`expect(COVERED_ARMS.length).toBe(14)` plus set equality). A case that silently stops running fails instead of quietly shrinking scope. Consequence for later drills: drive them with a file-level run, not `--test-name-pattern`, or that guard reddens for the wrong reason.

Also added an out-of-process guard: importing the port module in a real Node child must leave zero TCPSERVERWRAP/TCPWRAP/ChildProcess handles, so no port may listen, connect or spawn at import time.

implementationPlan.description: Implement adapters/jetbrains/src/host/jetbrains-host-ports.ts plus its one-line LF `.js` bridge (`export * from "./jetbrains-host-ports.ts";`, matching every sibling). Four port factories over node builtins only, each taking its configuration explicitly so nothing is discovered from ambient state: readInstalledDistributions(installRoot) using node:fs; probeDaemon(endpoint) using fetch, mapping ECONNREFUSED to NOT_LISTENING, ANY HTTP status including 401/403 to LISTENING, and everything else to UNDETERMINED with a sanitized detail; startDaemon(command, args, endpoint, bound) spawning detached via node:child_process and then re-probing until listening or the bound expires; openControlRoom(assetPath, opener) checking the asset on disk and delegating the open. Every port catches its own faults and returns an evidence arm — an exception escaping into the IDE event loop is the failure mode adapters/jetbrains/src/index.ts:76-87 documents and works around, and a port that throws forfeits the layer attribution. No detail string may carry a credential, a token, or an absolute host path. Keep the file under the 250-line target; if it approaches it, split the process ports from the filesystem ports rather than trimming comments.

BRIDGE: `printf 'export * from "./jetbrains-host-ports.ts";\n'`, verified by `od -c` (ends `s" ; \n`, no CR) and by substituting the module name into the sibling index.js — byte-identical shape. The package's bridge audit compares bytes through utf8, so a CRLF bridge would land in `wrongContent`.

THE FOUR PORTS, node builtins only, configuration passed explicitly so a test and a shipped plugin run the same path:
  readInstalledDistributions(installRoot) — readdir, filter *.json, SORT, read+JSON.parse each. EMPTY ON ANY FAULT, NEVER PARTIAL, and shape is deliberately NOT validated here: admitDistribution owns exact-shape admission and re-deciding it would fork the rule this boundary exists to protect. A parsed-but-wrong document reaches the gate and is refused MANIFEST_SCHEMA_INVALID, which is the correct division.
  probeDaemon(endpoint, timeoutMs) — fetch with AbortSignal.timeout. ANY HTTP status is LISTENING; only ECONNREFUSED is NOT_LISTENING; everything else UNDETERMINED.
  startDaemon(options) — spawn detached, stdio "ignore", windowsHide, unref. `spawn` and `error` are mutually exclusive so exactly one settles the launch.
  openControlRoom(assetPath, opener) — stat().isFile() first, so a missing installation NEVER reaches the OS opener; embedded is ALWAYS "UNAVAILABLE" because this host renders nothing.

FIVE THINGS I GOT RIGHT ONLY BY MEASURING, EACH ONE A REAL DEFECT AVOIDED:
1. THE ERROR CODE IS NOT ON THE THROWN ERROR. `fetch` rejects with a bare TypeError whose CAUSE carries ECONNREFUSED. Reading only the top-level error would have collapsed every transport fault into UNDETERMINED, and NOT_LISTENING — the arm that licenses a start — would have been unreachable in production while the test suite stayed green. codeOf() walks the cause chain with a cycle guard.
2. THE SANITIZER MUST BE A WHITELIST, NOT A BLACKLIST. Codes are admitted only if they match /^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]{1,39}$/; anything else becomes UNKNOWN. An OS error message can quote a full path, so filtering known-bad substrings would leak on the first message shape nobody predicted.
3. A CLAMPED PROBE INSIDE THE BOUND. The confirm loop recomputes the remaining time each iteration and clamps the probe's own timeout to it. Without that, a probe allowed to outrun the deadline defeats the bound from the inside — the loop would look bounded and would not be.
4. DEVIATION FROM THE PLAN, FORCED AND MEASURED: the plan's control-room OPENED detail was the asset path. That violates the plan's own "no detail string may carry an absolute host path" rule in the same step. The detail is now a fixed sentence; the opener still receives the real path, and the test asserts BOTH — opener called with the path, detail free of it.
5. DEVIATION IN THE TEST, FORCED: the UNDETERMINED case originally carried its secret in URL credentials (`http://user:token@host`). `fetch` rejects a credentialled URL before it connects, so that case would have settled on a parse error and never exercised the timeout it exists for — a vacuous pass. The secret now rides in the URL PATH, so the stalled-server timeout is genuinely exercised AND a real secret is present to leak. Detail asserted free of the token, the host, the port and "://".

Not fabricated anywhere: no detail is asserted to be safe in the abstract; each is asserted against material that is actually present in the input.

implementationPlan.description: Implement adapters/jetbrains/src/host/jetbrains-host.ts plus its `.js` bridge: the launcher, and nothing else. It imports createJetBrainsSession from the BARE `@moe/jetbrains-adapter` root — Node's self-reference rule resolves that through this package's own exports map, which is exactly what jetbrains-runtime-entrypoint.test.ts already proves — assembles the four ports from step 3 plus the JetBrainsDistributionExpectation this build was compiled against, and exposes start / uninstall / reconnect by delegating to the session. It contains NO lifecycle reducer, NO command authorization, NO board or rendering, and no state beyond the session handle: every product action and every pixel comes from the standalone control room, per task rail 1 and the adapter's own header. Add the host tests for composition: a successful run reaches the control room and reports the endpoint; a second concurrent open returns the SAME in-flight promise (the adapter's single-flight guarantee must survive composition, or a double-clicked tool window starts two daemons); uninstall mid-flight leaves no live handle and no port fires afterwards; and after uninstall a fresh reconnect succeeds. Refusal composition: an install root missing the DAEMON or CONTROL_ROOM component makes startup refuse with code DISTRIBUTION_MISMATCH BEFORE the discovery port is ever called — assert the probe port recorded zero calls, because 'before daemon access' is the load-bearing half of DoD 2 and a refusal that still probed proves nothing.

THE BARE ROOT IMPORT WORKS AND IS PROVEN BY THE COMPILER, NOT ASSUMED: jetbrains-host.ts does `import { createJetBrainsSession } from "@moe/jetbrains-adapter"` — the package's own name, resolved by Node's self-reference rule through its exports map. tsc exit 0 confirms self-name resolution; step 6's real-child probe will confirm it outside vitest, which is the only place it can actually fail.

THIN, AND PINNED AS AN EXACT SET. The host holds ONE piece of state (a nullable session handle) and exposes exactly four methods; `expect(Object.keys(host).sort()).toEqual(["endpoint","reconnect","start","uninstall"])` makes a reducer, a command entry point or a render hook added later a visible decision rather than a quiet widening. start and reconnect are deliberately the same sequence: the ADAPTER derives start-versus-reconnect from discovery evidence, and re-deciding it in the host would fork a decision that already has an owner.

COMPOSITION IS MEASURED AT THE SOCKET, NOT THROUGH A SPY. Each fixture runs a real node:http server that counts requests, a real install root of manifest documents, and a real asset file. "The probe never fired" is therefore a fact about the socket; a spy could have been wired wrongly and still agreed with itself.
  compose:success                     -> OK / CONTROL_ROOM_BROWSER_FALLBACK / layer null, host.endpoint() equals the live endpoint, opener called once.
  compose:single-flight               -> two synchronous start() calls return the SAME promise (toBe), and the server receives EXACTLY ONE request. A double-clicked tool window otherwise starts two daemons.
  compose:uninstall-mid-flight        -> UNKNOWN / DAEMON_STATE_UNKNOWN / IDE_ADAPTER, server request count 0, opener never called, endpoint() null. Teardown proven by absence at two real resources.
  compose:uninstall-then-reconnect    -> a fresh session succeeds after uninstall dropped the handle.
  compose:refuses-before-daemon-access-> install root with CONTROL_ROOM but no DAEMON gives exactly {code:"DISTRIBUTION_MISMATCH", ok:false, reason:"COMPONENT_SET_INCOMPLETE", refusedBy:"DISTRIBUTION_STARTUP"} AND the server request count is 0. "Before daemon access" is the load-bearing half of DoD 2; a refusal that had already probed would prove only that it refused eventually.
  compose:thin-surface                -> the exact four-method key set.

implementationPlan.description: Mutation drills. For each: sha256 first, edit with the Edit tool, confirm the anchor matched once, run only the named test, reverse the edit, confirm the sha256 is restored — never git checkout, which reverts to HEAD and would destroy uncommitted work in this shared worktree. D1: make the distribution discovery port return the manifests it COULD read when one entry is unreadable — the partial-set case reddens, proving the empty-on-fault rule is real and a missing component cannot be silently tolerated. D2: move the gate call after the daemon probe in the host composition — the zero-probe-calls assertion reddens, proving 'refuses before daemon access' is enforced rather than merely ordered by luck. D3: map an HTTP 401 to REFUSED instead of LISTENING — the reachability case reddens, proving the probe observes reachability and not authority. D4: remove the bound from the start confirm loop — the bounded-start case reddens or hangs; if it hangs, that IS the finding, and the test's own bound is what turns it into a named failure instead of a stalled suite. D5: drop the IDE_ADAPTER entry from the packaging INVENTORY — the inverted assertion reddens, proving the shipped component is asserted rather than assumed. D6: point one IDE_ADAPTER asset at a path that does not exist — the asset-resolves case reddens, which is the guard against a placeholder creeping back in. Read every failure message and confirm it names the assertion the drill targets.
